flags.reason: Same fasting advice given at lines 15, 24, 34 and 38 without responding to Barbara's replies; repeated pushing ignores her autonomy.
'You said the same thing last week' reads as a confrontation about past failure rather than exploring what got in the way.
'My sugar was better the weeks I ate earlier' is a clear change reason; coach did not reflect or explore it.
'I'm not going to change at my age' was met with a daughter question instead of a reflection or exploration of her values.
Summary says 'the parties' and '0 days in'; Barbara never named parties or a zero count, so the summary misstates her words.

score.summary: Coach repeatedly delivered the same fasting advice and pressed on the missed goal, which reduced partnership even though the call ended with a clear, self-chosen plan and a backup. Barbara's change talk (sugar improving, feeling better about herself, confidence at 4-5) went largely unreflected.
strengths: Line 49-51: scaling question for confidence, then asked 'Why a 4 and not a 1?' to draw out her reasons for change.
Line 53: planned for barriers with 'If the parties gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?' and Barbara produced a concrete fallback at line 54.
Line 57: set a concrete follow-up with a midweek text and a two-week check-in.
coaching_tips: Lines 15, 24, 34 and 38 repeat the same advice verbatim; replace repeats with a reflection or an open question about what Barbara wants to try.
Line 27 ('You said the same thing last week') sounds like a reprimand; try 'What has made the 5-day plan hard to keep?' instead.
Reflect change talk such as line 32 ('My sugar was better the weeks I ate earlier') and line 44 before moving on, e.g. 'Your energy and sugar levels matter to you.'
Respond to sustain talk at line 39 with a reflection, e.g. 'Changing eating habits feels like a lot at this point,' before asking about family support.
In the line 55 summary, use Barbara's own words and avoid adding details she did not say.
